title: Time-series satellite monitoring shows sisal condition shifts earlier, letting METL spot stress before conventional reporting cycles close the gap
subtitle: Continuous imagery produces an earlier signal of decline than periodic field reporting, enabling faster intervention on stressed sisal areas.

chart.annotation: The satellite signal turns down by Month 3, while conventional reporting lags and shows the sharper decline later.

insights.text: The satellite condition index falls from **82** in Month 1 to **76** by Month 3, surfacing deterioration before the conventional signal moves materially.
Conventional reporting stays at **82**, **82**, and **81** through Month 3, delaying visibility into the same emerging stress pattern.
By Month 6, both signals converge near **66** and **67**, showing that earlier satellite detection changes timing of action rather than the underlying field reality.
